episodes.201537: A severe thunderstorm dropped southeast out of Wyoming and produced one inch hail over northeast Weld County before it dissipated.
episodes.201539: A strong supercell thunderstorm tracked south-southeast across far northeast Weld, southwest Logan and northwest Washington Counties. The storms produced large hail, up to 3 inches in diameter and also three tornadoes across Logan and Washington Counties during the afternoon hours of May 23rd, including one EF-2 and one EF-1. Most of the observed damage was snapped power poles and trees. One single family residence sustained EF-1 damage, but there were no injuries reported. This supercell also produced a swath of golf ball to baseball sized hail, with one ICECHIP report of over 3 inch diameter hail in northern Washington county.
episodes.201641: Severe thunderstorm watch for Laramie County and most of the Nebraska Panhandle.
episodes.201960: Weak disturbances in the flow aloft caused isolated thunderstorms to develop in the Davis Mountains and Stockton Plateau during the afternoon. These thunderstorms eventually moved off of the higher terrain and tracked over the Trans-Pecos and Permian Basin. Though a couple of the storms produced severe wind gusts that afternoon, activity largely diminished by sunset.
episodes.202170: An upper-level shortwave trough generated thunderstorms on the warm side of a stationary front that was stretched across Central Texas. Some of these storms moved into South-Central Texas and produced large hail and a few damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202436: Thunderstorms developed by late afternoon of the 22nd across southwestern Oklahoma and western-north Texas. This activity was initiated near convective outflow boundaries from prior thunderstorms and enhanced by strong surface heating. The resulting environment featured strong instability, steep lapse rates, and favorable deep-layer wind shear for organized thunderstorms. Multiple splitting supercell thunderstorms emerged in this regime, producing widespread reports of large to very large hail during the evening.
episodes.202517: A severe thunderstorm produced large hail in Indiantown in Martin County.
episodes.202603: A cold front that moved into the region on May 21st had remained stalled over the Louisiana coast ror a couple days at this point. Strong daytime heating enhanced convective updrafts while temperatures aloft remain quite cool for the time of year. This environment was sufficient to support a severe thunderstorm with large hail.
episodes.202604: A cold front that moved into the region on May 21st had stalled over the Louisiana coast by the 22nd. Strong daytime heating enhanced convective updrafts while temperatures aloft remain quite cool for the time of year. This environment was sufficient to support severe thunderstorm downdrafts over the local marine areas.
episodes.202615: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred from Friday, May 23 through Tuesday, May 27, 2025. Total Rainfall amounts ranged between 2-5 inches, with localized amounts up to 8.6 inches.
episodes.202616: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred from Friday, May 23 through Tuesday, May 27, 2025. Total Rainfall amounts ranged between 2-4 inches in southeast Kansas, with up to 8.6 inches further east in Missouri. Additionally, a severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Crawford County.
episodes.202617: Scattered elevated thunderstorms produced a report of large hail across far northern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 23rd.
episodes.202812: A secondary cold front and upper level trough brought scattered severe thunderstorms to southeast Virginia in the late afternoon and evening. These storms mainly produced large hail, with a few reports of golf ball size hail and larger.
episodes.202816: A secondary cold front and upper level trough brought late evening storms to northeast North Carolina. One storm produced gusty winds on the Currituck Sound and North Carolina coastal waters.
episodes.202966: A complex upper trough over the Atlantic coast combined with active convective cumulus cloud lines over the Upper Florida Keys and week inhibition resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorm producing isolated gale-force wind gusts and an isolated waterspout.
episodes.202968: Cloud lines along the oceanside of the middle and lower Florida Keys under a deep mean-layer ridge produced a couple waterspouts in Hawk Channel.
episodes.202977: The combination of surface instability and an upper level area of low pressure resulted in severe thunderstorms that produced very strong winds and localized wind damage. In addition, some of these severe storms produced very heavy rainfall.
episodes.203064: On May 22, strong to severe thunderstorms developed across western North Texas, driven by a northward-moving warm front and a southward-propagating upper-level disturbance. Areas extending from Gainesville southwest to Eastland experienced occasional severe weather impacts, including large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.203575: Ample moisture, a decaying surface boundary, and a disturbance at the mid to upper levels of the atmosphere supported the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over southern Florida in the afternoon and evening hours of May 23, 2025.

The formation of this tornado was captured well by storm chaser video. The tornado did not have a coherent damage path. There was sporadic damage south of the South Platte River, primarily to a trio of grain silos. Two silos had their tops removed, one was shifted off the pad, another was destroyed. One off duty NWS employee confirmed the location of the tornado as it crossed Logan County Road R just south of County Road 59. The tornado dissipated just southwest of the Prewitt Reservoir with no evidence it crossed I-76.

Well documented tornado that moved south parallel to CO-63, remaining generally in open areas 2-3 miles west of CO-63. We obtained the width (400 yds) of the tornado based on power poles snapped along County Road 50. One single family residence was struck with minor damage to the house, and significant damage to all outbuildings and trees on the property, consistent with EF-1 damage. Debris from the property was carried approximately one mile to the south-southwest. Further south of the damaged property, power poles were snapped and thrown a considerable distance (25 yds), consistent with EF-2 intensity. The power poles were on the west side of AA, just north of County Road 48. Video evidence and the results of the storm survey, suggest that the tornado dissipated just before 6 PM MDT.
